question:
I have the Standard plan in the image below, and I just uploaded 60 equally sized files and got a message that I'm 100GB over the limit. I have 980 more files of the same size to upload. What is the average additional cost per file in dollar that goes over my current plan limit rounded to the nearest cent if I have to upgrade to the minimum possible plan to store them all? Answer with the following format: x.xx

history.name: CloudStoragePricing_Expert
history.content: I'll extract the storage tiers and prices from the image, compute the file size from the overage signal, figure out total storage for all files, and choose the smallest plan that fits. Then I'll derive the average additional cost per over-limit file. Computer_terminal, please OCR the image so I can parse the details.

history.name: CloudStoragePricing_Expert
history.content: Key points from the image: Standard has 2 TB, Plus 10 TB, Premium 50 TB. Pricing shows 9.99, 19.99, 39.99. Using the overage message: after 60 files, you're 100 GB over Standard's cap. So 60 files = 2,000 GB + 100 GB = 2,100 GB. Each file ≈ 2,100/60 = 35 GB. Total files = 60 + 980 = 1,040. Total storage ≈ 1,040 × 35 GB = 36,400 GB = 36.4 TB. Minimum plan to cover 36.4 TB is Premium. Price delta vs Standard = 39.99 − 9.99 = 30. We'll next compute average additional cost per file that exceeds the Standard limit.

history.name: Validation_Expert
history.content: The storage math looks consistent: file size 35 GB, total 36.4 TB, Premium needed. However, the pricing cadence isn't stated in your summary (are those monthly or annual figures?). To avoid underestimating, I'll annualize the price delta. Standard capacity in files: 2,000/35 ≈ 57 files. Over-limit files: 1,040 − 57 = 983. Compute (30 × 12) / 983 and round to nearest cent.

history.name: CloudStoragePricing_Expert
history.content: Running a quick calculation for annualized delta per over-limit file: 360/983. Computer_terminal, please evaluate 360/983 and report the numeric result.

history.name: Validation_Expert
history.content: 0.3664318418 rounds to 0.37 to the nearest cent. Proceed with 0.37.

mistake_reason: At step 2, CloudStoragePricing_Expert had access to the OCR output that explicitly included the pricing unit “/month,” but they summarized the plans and prices while omitting the “per month” cadence. This information withholding (FM-2.4) deprived the Validation_Expert of a critical unit, leading them to assume annualized pricing (multiplying by 12) and compute the average additional cost per file using yearly cost instead of the monthly cost required by the image and task. The miscommunication across agents caused the final wrong answer (0.37 instead of 0.03).
